intro.author: Not named. Jewish tradition credits most of it to Joshua (24:26 says he wrote 'in the book of the law of God'); his death and notes such as 'unto this day' show later hands. Many scholars see it as part of a larger history running from Deuteronomy to Kings.
intro.written: Uncertain. Traditionally soon after the events; many scholars date its final form to the 600s–500s BC
intro.audience: The people of Israel, remembering how they came to live in the land God promised
intro.setting: After Moses dies, Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan into Canaan, a land of walled towns each ruled by its own king. The book tells of campaigns in the center, south and north, then the dividing of the land among the tribes. The events are traditionally dated around 1400 BC; many scholars place them in the 1200s BC.
intro.purpose: To show that God kept his promise of land to Abraham's descendants, and to call Israel to stay faithful to the covenant once they lived there.
intro.bigIdea: God kept every promise he made, and his people must choose to serve him alone.
